the first run of kl-to-better-teacher that I did. Used coefficient 0.15 which got the model to prioritize lowering kl_policy_base (.27 to .06) but also lowered reward. It could be that continuing to train from this is is promising, but idk. 2 modifications i did was try to kl relative to a little-trained student, so we are not KLing relative to something which has format errs, etc + lower penalty coeff from 0.15 to 0.075, .035). unclear how good this actually worked, since we did not try distilling to the student

this seems like a pretty succefull Q4Bi runs! starting from <hidden> in stage 2. well, actually, hidden lengths are not quite at 0, although we get very low sus, high backdoor_test_passed. currently the model is accepting a penalty of -.3 for hidden lengths of 70. this actually warrents continuing to train to see <hidden> go completely away, which it should eventually as the penalty grows enormous. what seems to work so well about Q4BI is that it doesn't go crazy. <hidden>  lengths remain limited and not the entire response. It doesn't have the same problem we are seeing with the others of being super sensetive to <hidden> reward / penalty (that they use <hidden> on everything with very long sequence length or quickly don't use it at all. it seems also that Q4BI is better able to put the reasoning that should be in <hidden> in <hidden>
